title: docs: the worker.reference.md LANDING rule still says "use no git command"; align it with task-b5c8fd34's resume prompt (read-only git allowlist, merged-tree verification)
description:
Follow-up to task-b5c8fd341d4f48f89f5056b176622428. That task rewrites the LANDING-CONFLICT/LANDING-RETRY resume prompt in scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}. It drops "no git commands" and appends one identical rule (sh `resume_rule`, ps1 `$resumeRule`) to both lines:
- HEAD can lack the merged target.
- A verification snapshot built from HEAD (`git archive HEAD`, or a clone checked out at HEAD) is built from the worktree's tracked files instead.
- Git stays read-only: only git status, git diff, git log, git show, git ls-files and git rev-parse may run. Every git write stays forbidden.

docs/roles/worker.reference.md :97 (the LANDING rule) still says "Edit files only: use no git command (commit, merge, reset, checkout, abort) ... Then re-run the plan's verification command". That now contradicts the prompt. A worker who reads the reference gets the same mixed signal that stalled WT-14's resume (msg-c9029b23).

This row only aligns the docs with the landed wrapper text: read the landed `resume_rule` line, never a planned copy. The doc is vendored, so packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts must be regenerated in a clone with history and applied with the Edit tool (Serena convention-role-doc-edits-regenerate-initfiles). worker.md's pointer "(edit files only; leave git to the wrapper)" still holds for git writes and may stay unchanged. The dated design record docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md stays out of scope.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/worker.reference.md's LANDING rule no longer says "use no git command"; it names the same read-only allowlist as the landed resume rule (git status, git diff, git log, git show, git ls-files, git rev-parse), keeps every git write forbidden, and tells the worker to build a HEAD-based verification snapshot from the worktree's tracked files.

packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts is regenerated from the edited doc in a clone with history (marker sha and SHIPPED_ROLE_BODY_SHAS), and its diff touches only the worker.reference.md entry.

npm run lint passes, and packages/moe-daemon src/util/initFiles.test.ts, src/util/targetedContextGuidance.test.ts and src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts pass in a Linux snapshot, with the exact commands and counts in the completion evidence.
